close_reason: Fixed in commit d0a0bd4. MetadataChangesParams.filter_metadata_type now carries an explicit semantics note distinguishing None (disable filter, return all types) from Some(vec![]) (legal empty array matching no @type values per draft §3.3, server returns empty arrays).
description: src/methods/mod.rs:49-53 docstring on filter_metadata_type doesn't address the empty-Vec case. Per draft §3.3 'If specified, the response MUST include only changes to Metadata objects whose @type property value is in the specified array.' An empty array therefore matches nothing — the response will contain only an empty created/updated/destroyed. This is a real footgun: a caller writing Some(vec![]) (perhaps because they computed the filter list and it came out empty) gets a silently-empty response rather than 'all types'. Audience: caller trying to debug 'why are no changes coming through'. Fix: one-sentence doc comment 'Note: Some(vec![]) means "match no @type values" per draft §3.3 — use None to disable filtering instead.' Either as a behaviour note on the field, or as runtime InvalidArgument guard converting Some(vec![]) → InvalidArgument. Defence-in-depth option is more aggressive than this crate's other guards; doc-comment is the minimum bar.
title: MetadataChangesParams: empty filterMetadataType array semantics not documented
